sections.h2: Which Iredell County offices take deeds for recording?
sections.html:
Two sites handle recording for Iredell County, one in Statesville and one in Mooresville, and staff there work weekdays from opening at eight in the morning until five in the afternoon, according to the county staff directory.

  • Statesville site: 211 Constitution Ln, Statesville, NC 28677, telephone 704-872-7468
  • Mooresville site: 610 E Center Ave, Mooresville, NC 28115, telephone 704-663-4533
  • Shared fax line: 704-878-5426

The same staff issue certified birth and death certificates, marriage licenses and copies of military discharges, and they administer notary oaths. Nearly everything held there is open to any member of the public. The one stated exception is military discharges.

A seller in this county will mostly meet this office through your closing attorney, who delivers the signed deed and the buyer's deed of trust. Afterward, a call to either site confirms that both papers made the record and shows the order in which they were filed.

sections.h2: What role does recording play when a house sells?
sections.html:
Recording makes the transfer effective against outsiders. The staff index the deed and the lender's deed of trust under the names of the parties, and the filing time fixes who stands first in line.

North Carolina's recording statute says a conveyance does not bind lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered where the land lies. Priority then runs by time of registration. That explains why a closing is not finished when pens come down, and why attorneys wait for confirmation of recording before releasing funds.

Iredell staff are clear about what they cannot do. They may not draft a deed or assist in drafting one, and they may not search title or offer a title opinion. Taking a name on or off a deed takes a fresh deed that is drafted, notarized and recorded, so most owners bring in a lawyer.

Court judgments sit elsewhere. The county FAQ tells people to look for them with the Clerk of Court at 704-832-6600, and it explains that a judgment lasts ten years, can be renewed for ten more, and attaches to land you own or later acquire. Before you sign a sale contract, ask your attorney to check for any entry against you.

sections.h2: What are the Iredell County filing charges?
sections.html:
A routine instrument is $26.00 for pages one through fifteen, and each page past fifteen adds $4.00, while a loan security document runs $64.00 for its first thirty-five pages. Those amounts come from G.S. 161-10, which applies in all one hundred counties alike.

Fees charged for filing in Iredell County, as listed in G.S. 161-10
Filing typeCharge
General instrument, pages 1 to 15$26.00
Every added page$4.00
Mortgage or deed of trust, pages 1 to 35$64.00
Release or cancellation of a deed of trustNone
Plat sheet$21.00
Certified copy, opening page$5.00
Oversize or irregular document$25.00 extra

Source: North Carolina General Statutes, section 161-10, which calls the schedule complete and exclusive and collects it up front.

For copies of what is already recorded, the county posts its own prices on its FAQ page: a deed copy at $.25 per page and a printed copy of a recorded map at $1.00. Mailed copies carry an additional charge, so call before you send a request.

sections.h2: Which party owes transfer tax on an Iredell County deed?
sections.html:
The person transferring the property owes it, and it must be paid to the Register ahead of the deed reaching the record. The tax rate is $1.00 on every $500 of price, and a leftover fraction counts as a full $500.

Under the excise tax statute, half the receipts stay in the Iredell general fund and the rest travel to the state revenue department. The Iredell FAQ illustrates the rate with its own sample: a $2,000 land purchase carries $4.00 of tax at filing.

The figure is based on the price or value of the interest passing. Because the statute places the duty on the seller, read your settlement statement for this line and ask your attorney how the contract handles it. A seller who accepts a cash offer still sees the same tax, since it follows the deed and not the buyer.

sections.h2: Where can I look up Iredell County land records online?
sections.html:
The county Register page links to a records search covering deeds, deeds of trust, plats and powers of attorney. Iredell says land records run from December 1788 to the present and that state law requires indexing by party name.

Its Land Records page offers a search guide, indexing rules and a separate guide for property recorded before 1964. A notice on the online portal says the system is being tested during a software change, that results may be incomplete, and that the portal is not an official record. For a sale, request a certified copy from the office instead of printing from the screen.

  • Find an owner: use the tax office GIS maps, or call 704-878-3020 for help with them.
  • Proof a mortgage is paid: the lender files a certificate of satisfaction, and the staff will mail or email you a copy.
  • Replace a lost deed: give names and a purchase year, and a copy costs $.25 per page.

Two plain-language answers from the same FAQ help sellers. A deed moves ownership, usually from seller to buyer, while a deed of trust ties the borrower, the lender and a neutral trustee together to secure a loan. The office also explains that a lender's title policy protects the lender, while an owner's policy is optional and protects you against defects a title search missed, and it recommends carrying both.

sections.h2: Is property tax paid through the Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
No. Iredell County Tax Administration in Statesville bills and collects it, and the Register only records instruments. The two still meet at a sale, since a buyer's attorney expects the tax account to be current.

The collector tells owners that payoff at the closing table is available on request, and that a prepayment can be taken at last year's rate if the new bill is not out. The 2026 county rate is .50 per $100 on the county rates page, with towns such as Statesville and Mooresville adding theirs.

Ownership for tax purposes is fixed on January 1. A seller who closes later keeps the liability for that year's bill unless the contract moves it, so look at the proration line on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: How big is the Iredell County housing market?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts puts Iredell County at 211,798 people as of mid-2025, spread across 574.41 square miles and roughly 93,711 housing units.

  • Homeowners occupy 71.9 percent of occupied units (2020-2024).
  • A typical owner-held house is worth $321,400, and borrowers report median monthly housing costs of $1,714.
  • Median household income reads $81,419, and the middle gross rent is $1,252 a month.
  • Local governments issued 1,835 building permits in 2025.

faqs.q: Which Iredell County office should I use to record a deed?
faqs.a: Either one. The Statesville site at 211 Constitution Ln and the Mooresville site at 610 E Center Ave both accept recordings on weekdays between eight and five.

faqs.q: What is the filing charge for a deed in Iredell County?
faqs.a: A routine instrument is $26.00 up to fifteen pages, and every extra page adds $4.00. Deeds of trust start at $64.00 for thirty-five pages, then add the same $4.00 per extra page.

faqs.q: Who bears the excise tax on an Iredell County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it before the deed is filed, at a dollar per $500 of value. Your contract and closing statement show how it is handled.

faqs.q: Can Iredell County staff prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. State law bars them from drafting deeds. Hire a North Carolina attorney, then bring the signed, notarized deed in for filing.

faqs.q: Where do I check for a judgment against my Iredell County property?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Court at 704-832-6600 holds them, and the Register does not. A judgment lasts ten years and may be extended for ten more.
